title.zh: 卷二 本紀第二 武帝中
title.raw: 卷二 本紀第二 武帝中 Volume 2 Annals 2: Emperor Wu 2

sentences.zh: 七年正月己未，振旅于京師。

translations.literal: In the first month of the seventh year, on the day jiwei, he led the army back to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the seventh year (411), on the day jiwei, Gaozu marched his troops back to the capital.

sentences.zh: 改授大將軍、揚州牧，給班劍二十人，本官悉如故，固辭。

translations.literal: He was reassigned as Grand General and Governor of Yangzhou, granted twenty ceremonial swords, and all his original offices were left unchanged; he firmly declined.
translations.idiomatic: The court offered him Grand General and Governor of Yangzhou, with twenty ceremonial swords and all his old posts unchanged. He refused.

sentences.zh: 凡南北征伐戰亡者，並列上賻贈。

translations.literal: All who had died in battle on the northern and southern campaigns were to be listed and presented for funeral subsidies.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered a full list of those killed in the northern and southern campaigns, with funeral grants for each.

sentences.zh: 尸喪未反，遣主帥迎接，致還本土。

translations.literal: Where the dead had not yet been brought back, he sent the commanders to receive them and return them to their native districts.
translations.idiomatic: Where bodies had not yet come home, he sent the field commanders to escort them back to their home districts.

sentences.zh: 二月，盧循至番禺，為孫季高所破，收餘眾南走。

translations.literal: In the second month, Lu Xun reached Panyu, was defeated by Sun Jigao, gathered his remaining forces, and fled south.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month Lu Xun reached Panyu. Sun Jigao defeated him; he gathered what was left of his army and fled south.

sentences.zh: 劉藩、孟懷玉斬徐道覆于始興。

translations.literal: Liu Fan and Meng Huaiyu beheaded Xu Daofu at Shixing.
translations.idiomatic: At Shixing, Liu Fan and Meng Huaiyu beheaded Xu Daofu.

sentences.zh: 晉自中興以來，治綱大弛，權門并兼，強弱相凌，百姓流離，不得保其產業。

translations.literal: Since the Jin restoration, the bonds of governance had greatly slackened; powerful houses annexed one another, the strong bullied the weak, and the common people were displaced and could not keep their livelihoods.
translations.idiomatic: Since the Jin court moved south, government had grown lax. Great families swallowed their neighbors, the strong preyed on the weak, and ordinary people lost their homes and could not hold on to their land.

sentences.zh: 桓玄頗欲釐改，竟不能行。

translations.literal: Huan Xuan had wished somewhat to reform this, but in the end could not carry it out.
translations.idiomatic: Huan Xuan had tried to set things right, but never managed to.

sentences.zh: 公既作輔，大示軌則，豪強肅然，遠近知禁。

translations.literal: Once Gaozu had become regent, he displayed great norms; the powerful were awed into order, and near and far learned what was forbidden.
translations.idiomatic: Once Gaozu took power as regent, he laid down clear rules. The mighty fell silent, and everyone, near and far, knew the law.

sentences.zh: 至是會稽餘姚虞亮復藏匿亡命千餘人。

translations.literal: At this time Yu Liang of Yuyao in Kuaiji again harbored more than a thousand fugitives.
translations.idiomatic: By then Yu Liang of Yuyao in Kuaiji was again sheltering over a thousand fugitives.

sentences.zh: 公誅亮，免會稽內史司馬休之。

translations.literal: Gaozu executed Liang and dismissed Sima Xiuzhi, Interior Minister of Kuaiji.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu had Liang executed and removed Sima Xiuzhi as Interior Minister of Kuaiji.

sentences.zh: 天子又申前命，公固辭。

translations.literal: The Son of Heaven again pressed the earlier appointment upon him, and Gaozu firmly declined.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor pressed the earlier honors on him again. Gaozu refused.

sentences.zh: 於是改授太尉、中書監，乃受命。

translations.literal: Thereupon he was reassigned as Grand Commandant and Supervisor of the Masters of Writing, and then accepted the commission.
translations.idiomatic: He was then made Grand Commandant and Supervisor of the Masters of Writing, and this time he accepted.

sentences.zh: 奉送黃鉞，解冀州。

translations.literal: The court presented the yellow battle-axe, and he relinquished Jizhou.
translations.idiomatic: The court sent him the yellow battle-axe; he gave up Jizhou.

sentences.zh: 交州刺史杜慧度斬盧循，傳首京師。

translations.literal: Inspector of Jiaozhou Du Huidu beheaded Lu Xun and sent his head to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Du Huidu, Inspector of Jiaozhou, killed Lu Xun and sent his head to the capital.

sentences.zh: 先是諸州郡所遣秀才、孝廉，多非其人，公表天子，申明舊制，依舊策試。

translations.literal: Previously the Recommended Scholars and Filial and Incorrupt candidates sent up by the provinces and commanderies had often not been fit men; Gaozu memorialized the Son of Heaven, clarifying the old regulations and restoring the written examinations as before.
translations.idiomatic: Provincial nominees for office had often been unworthy. Gaozu petitioned the throne to restore the old examination system.

sentences.zh: 征西將軍、荊州刺史道規疾患求歸，八年四月，改授豫州刺史，以後將軍、豫州刺史劉毅代之。

translations.literal: General Who Pacifies the West and Inspector of Jingzhou Daogui, ill, asked to return; in the fourth month of the eighth year he was reassigned as Inspector of Yuzhou, and Rear General and Inspector of Yuzhou Liu Yi replaced him.
translations.idiomatic: Daogui, General Who Pacifies the West and Inspector of Jingzhou, fell ill and asked to come home. In the fourth month of the eighth year (412) he was made Inspector of Yuzhou; Liu Yi, Rear General and Inspector of Yuzhou, took his place in Jing.

sentences.zh: 毅與公俱舉大義，興復晉室，自謂京城、廣陵，功業足以相抗。

translations.literal: Yi had raised the great cause together with Gaozu and restored the Jin house; he considered that his achievements at the capital and at Guangling were enough to rival Gaozu's.
translations.idiomatic: Yi had joined Gaozu in restoring the Jin dynasty and thought his deeds at the capital and at Guangling matched Gaozu's own.

sentences.zh: 雖權事推公，而心不服也。

translations.literal: Though in power he deferred to Gaozu, in his heart he was not content.
translations.idiomatic: He yielded to Gaozu in public, but in his heart he would not submit.

sentences.zh: 毅既有雄才大志，厚自矜許，朝士素望者多歸之。

translations.literal: Yi possessed great talent and high ambition and thought highly of himself; many courtiers of long-standing repute turned to him.
translations.idiomatic: Yi was talented, ambitious, and vain. Many senior officials looked to him instead.

sentences.zh: 與尚書僕射謝混、丹陽尹郗僧施並深相結。

translations.literal: He was deeply allied with Vice Director of the Masters of Writing Xie Hun and Chief of Danyang Xi Sengshi.
translations.idiomatic: He was close to Xie Hun, Vice Director of the Masters of Writing, and Xi Sengshi, Chief of Danyang.

sentences.zh: 及西鎮江陵，豫州舊府，多割以自隨，請僧施為南蠻校尉。

translations.literal: When he went west to Jiangling, the old offices of Yuzhou were largely carved up for his own use, and he requested that Sengshi be made Commander Who Pacifies the Southern Man.
translations.idiomatic: Once he held Jiangling in the west, he took over much of the old Yuzhou establishment and asked that Sengshi be made Commander Who Pacifies the Southern Man.

sentences.zh: 既知毅不能居下，終為異端，密圖之。

translations.literal: Knowing that Yi could not remain subordinate and would in the end become a rebel, he secretly laid plans against him.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu saw that Yi would never stay below him and would turn rebel; he began to plot in secret.

sentences.zh: 毅至西，稱疾篤，表求從弟兗州刺史藩以為副貳，偽許焉。

translations.literal: When Yi reached the west he claimed grave illness and memorialized, asking that his younger cousin Fan, Inspector of Yanzhou, be made his deputy; this was falsely granted.
translations.idiomatic: Yi reached the west, claimed to be gravely ill, and asked that his cousin Fan, Inspector of Yanzhou, be made his deputy. Gaozu pretended to agree.

sentences.zh: 九月，藩入朝，公命收藩及謝混，並於獄賜死。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, when Fan entered court, Gaozu ordered Fan and Xie Hun seized and both were granted death in prison.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month Fan came to court. Gaozu had him and Xie Hun arrested and executed in prison.

sentences.zh: 自表討毅。

translations.literal: He himself memorialized to campaign against Yi.
translations.idiomatic: He then memorialized to take the field against Yi.

sentences.zh: 又假黃鉞，率諸軍西征。

translations.literal: He was also lent the yellow battle-axe and led the armies west on campaign.
translations.idiomatic: He was given the yellow battle-axe and marched west at the head of the armies.

sentences.zh: 以前鎮軍將軍司馬休之為平西將軍、荊州刺史，兗州刺史道憐鎮丹徒，豫州刺史諸葛長民監太尉留府事，加太尉司馬、丹陽尹劉穆之建威將軍，配以實力。

translations.literal: Former General Who Guards the Army Sima Xiuzhi was made General Who Pacifies the West and Inspector of Jingzhou; Inspector of Yanzhou Daoling garrisoned Dantu; Inspector of Yuzhou Zhuge Changmin oversaw the Grand Commandant's headquarters; and Grand Commandant Marshal and Chief of Danyang Liu Muzhi was made General Who Establishes Might, each posted with real force.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Xiuzhi became General Who Pacifies the West and Inspector of Jingzhou; Daoling held Dantu; Changmin ran the capital in Gaozu's absence; Muzhi was made General Who Establishes Might—all with real troops behind them.

sentences.zh: 壬午，發自京師。

translations.literal: On the day renwu he set out from the capital.
translations.idiomatic: On the day renwu he marched out from the capital.

sentences.zh: 遣參軍王鎮惡、龍驤將軍蒯恩前襲江陵。

translations.literal: He sent Staff Officer Wang Zhen'e and Dragon-Chariot General Kuai En ahead to strike Jiangling.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Wang Zhen'e and Kuai En ahead to take Jiangling.

sentences.zh: 十月，鎮惡剋江陵，毅及黨與皆伏誅。

translations.literal: In the tenth month, Zhen'e took Jiangling; Yi and his partisans were all executed.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month Zhen'e took Jiangling. Yi and his followers were all put to death.

sentences.zh: 十一月己卯，公至江陵，下書曰：

translations.literal: On the day jimao of the eleventh month, Gaozu reached Jiangling and issued a proclamation, saying:
translations.idiomatic: On the day jimao in the eleventh month Gaozu reached Jiangling and issued a proclamation:

sentences.zh: 夫去弊拯民，必存簡恕，捨網修綱，雖煩易理。

translations.literal: "To remove abuses and save the people, one must preserve simplicity and forbearance; to cast aside the net and repair the cords, though troublesome, is easy to justify in principle."
translations.idiomatic: "To cure abuses and help the people, government must stay simple and humane. Tightening the law after years of disorder is hard work, but it is the right course."

sentences.zh: 江、荊彫殘，刑政多闕，頃年事故，綏撫未週。

translations.literal: Jiang and Jing were wasted and maimed; penal administration had many gaps; in recent years, because of upheaval, pacification had not been thorough.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang and Jing were devastated; justice was patchy; years of turmoil had left the region half-settled.

sentences.zh: 遂令百姓疲匱，歲月滋甚，財傷役困，慮不幸生。

translations.literal: Thus the common people grew exhausted and impoverished, month by month the harm deepened, wealth was injured and corvée labor distressed, and I feared misfortune might arise.
translations.idiomatic: The people grew poorer every month, taxes and labor broke them, and I feared worse would follow.

sentences.zh: 凋殘之餘，而不減舊，刻剝徵求，不循政道。

translations.literal: On what remained of the wasted land, levies were not reduced from old levels; exactions and requisitions did not follow the way of government.
translations.idiomatic: Even on ruined ground the old levies stood. Officials squeezed the people without regard to law.

sentences.zh: 宰莅之司，或非良榦，未能菲躬儉，[1]苟求盈給，積習生常，漸不知改。

translations.literal: The officials who presided over districts were not always capable men; they could not restrain themselves in frugality, [1] but sought only to fill quotas; accumulated habit became custom, and gradually they no longer knew how to change.
translations.idiomatic: Many local magistrates were unfit. They would not live plainly [1] but chased every quota until waste became habit and reform seemed impossible.

sentences.zh: 近因戎役，來涉二州，踐境親民，愈見其瘼，思欲振其所急，卹其所苦。

translations.literal: Recently, because of the military campaign, I have come to these two provinces; treading the borders and facing the people, I have seen their afflictions all the more clearly, and I wish to rouse what is urgent and relieve what is bitter.
translations.idiomatic: This campaign has brought me into both provinces. Seeing the people myself, I know their distress and mean to ease what hurts them most.

sentences.zh: 凡租稅調役，悉宜以見戶為正。

translations.literal: All rent, tax, and corvée levies should be based entirely on registered households as they stand.
translations.idiomatic: All rent, tax, and labor duties shall be assessed only on actual registered households.

sentences.zh: 州郡縣屯田池塞，諸非軍國所資，利入守宰者，今一切除之。

translations.literal: Garrison fields, ponds, and passes in the provinces, commanderies, and counties—whatever did not serve military or state needs but whose profits went to the guarding magistrates—are now all abolished.
translations.idiomatic: Provincial garrison farms, ponds, and toll stations that served private profit rather than the army or the state are abolished at once.

sentences.zh: 州郡縣吏，皆依尚書定制實戶置。

translations.literal: Officials in the provinces, commanderies, and counties shall all be appointed according to the Masters of Writing's fixed quotas for actual households.
translations.idiomatic: Provincial, commandery, and county staffs shall be set only at the numbers the Masters of Writing allow for real households.

sentences.zh: 臺調癸卯梓材，庚子皮毛，可悉停省，別量所出。

translations.literal: The court requisitions of guimao timber and gengzi hides may all be halted and reduced; other sources shall be measured instead.
translations.idiomatic: Court demands for guimao timber and gengzi hides are suspended; other supplies will be found.

sentences.zh: 巴陵均折度支，依舊兵運。

translations.literal: The Ba-ling equalization and expenditure office shall follow the old military transport rules.
translations.idiomatic: The Ba-ling equalization office shall return to the old military transport system.

sentences.zh: 原五歲刑已下。

translations.literal: Pardon all punishments of five years or less.
translations.idiomatic: All sentences of five years or less are pardoned.

sentences.zh: 凡所質錄賊家餘口，亦悉原放。

translations.literal: All dependents of rebel households held as pledges are likewise to be released.
translations.idiomatic: Dependents taken hostage from rebel families are also freed.

sentences.zh: 以荊州十郡為湘州，公乃進督。

translations.literal: Ten commanderies of Jingzhou were made into Xiangzhou, and Gaozu then advanced as supervisor.
translations.idiomatic: Ten commanderies of Jing were split off as Xiang province, and Gaozu took overall supervision.

sentences.zh: [2]以西陽太守朱齡石為益州刺史，率眾伐蜀。

translations.literal: [2] Administrator of Xiyang Zhu Lingshi was made Inspector of Yizhou and led the armies to attack Shu.
translations.idiomatic: [2] Zhu Lingshi, Administrator of Xiyang, was made Inspector of Yizhou and marched against Shu.

sentences.zh: 進公太傅、揚州牧，加羽葆鼓吹，班劍二十人。

translations.literal: Gaozu was promoted to Grand Tutor and Governor of Yangzhou, with feathered canopy, drums, and whistles, and twenty ceremonial swords.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu was made Grand Tutor and Governor of Yangzhou, with imperial music and twenty ceremonial swords.

sentences.zh: 九年二月乙丑，公至自江陵。

translations.literal: On the day yichou of the second month of the ninth year, Gaozu returned from Jiangling.
translations.idiomatic: On the day yichou in the second month of the ninth year (413) Gaozu returned from Jiangling.

sentences.zh: 初諸葛長民貪淫驕橫，為士民所患苦，公以其同大義，優容之。

translations.literal: Earlier, Zhuge Changmin had been greedy, licentious, arrogant, and overbearing, a affliction to scholars and commoners; Gaozu, because he had shared the great cause, treated him with forbearance.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuge Changmin had long been greedy, brutal, and hated by the people. Gaozu had tolerated him because they had fought together for the dynasty.

sentences.zh: 劉毅既誅，長民謂所親曰：「昔年醢彭越，今年誅韓信，禍其至矣。

translations.literal: After Liu Yi was executed, Changmin said to those close to him: "Last year they minced Peng Yue; this year they kill Han Xin—disaster is upon me.
translations.idiomatic: After Yi died, Changmin told his intimates, "Last year Peng Yue was boiled; this year Han Xin is killed. My turn is coming.

sentences.zh: 」將謀作亂。

translations.literal: " He was about to plot rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: " He began to plot rebellion.

sentences.zh: 公克期至京邑，而每淹留不進。

translations.literal: Gaozu had set a date to reach the capital, yet each day he delayed and did not advance.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu had named a day to reach the capital, but lingered on the road.

sentences.zh: 公卿以下頻日奉候於新亭，長民亦驟出。

translations.literal: From the Three Dukes down, for days on end they went to wait upon him at Xinting; Changmin too came out repeatedly in haste.
translations.idiomatic: For days the highest officials waited on him at Xinting. Changmin kept hurrying out to meet him.

sentences.zh: 既而公輕舟密至，已還東府矣。

translations.literal: Presently Gaozu came secretly in a light boat and was already back at the eastern headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: Then Gaozu slipped in by light boat and was already back at his eastern headquarters.

sentences.zh: 長民到門。

translations.literal: Changmin came to the gate.
translations.idiomatic: Changmin came to the gate.

sentences.zh: 引前，卻人閑語，凡平生於長民所不盡者，皆與及之。

translations.literal: Gaozu drew him forward, dismissed the attendants, and in private conversation went over everything in their lives that he had never yet said to Changmin.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu brought him in, sent everyone else away, and spoke with him at length about everything he had never yet said between them.

sentences.zh: 長民甚說。

translations.literal: Changmin was greatly pleased.
translations.idiomatic: Changmin was delighted.

sentences.zh: 已密命左右壯士丁旿等自幔後出，於坐拉焉。

translations.literal: He had already secretly ordered the strong men at his side, Ding Wu and the rest, to come out from behind the curtain and seize him where he sat.
translations.idiomatic: He had already told his strongmen, Ding Wu and the rest, to slip out from behind the curtain and seize him in his seat.

sentences.zh: 長民墜牀，又於地毆之，死於牀側。

translations.literal: Changmin fell from the couch; they beat him again on the ground, and he died beside the couch.
translations.idiomatic: Changmin fell from the couch. They beat him on the floor until he died beside it.

sentences.zh: 輿尸付廷尉。

translations.literal: His body was placed in a cart and handed over to the Minister of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: The body was carted to the Minister of Justice.

sentences.zh: 并誅其弟黎民。

translations.literal: His younger brother Limin was also executed.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Limin was executed as well.

sentences.zh: 旿驍勇有氣力，時人為之語曰：「勿跋扈，付丁旿。」

translations.literal: Wu was fierce and brave and full of strength; at the time people made a saying of it: "Do not act the bully—hand it to Ding Wu."
translations.idiomatic: Wu was famously fierce. People said, "Don't play the tyrant—leave it to Ding Wu."

sentences.zh: 先是山湖川澤，皆為豪強所專，小民薪採漁釣，皆責稅直，至是禁斷之。

translations.literal: Previously, mountains, lakes, rivers, and marshes had all been monopolized by the powerful; common people gathering firewood, fishing, or cutting reeds all paid a tax; now this was forbidden and cut off.
translations.idiomatic: Powerful families had seized lakes, rivers, and hills; even firewood and fishing carried a fee. That was now forbidden.

sentences.zh: 時民居未一，公表曰：

translations.literal: At the time the people were not yet settled in one place; Gaozu memorialized, saying:
translations.idiomatic: The people were still unsettled. Gaozu submitted a memorial:

sentences.zh: 臣聞先王制治，九土攸序，分境畫疆，各安其居。

translations.literal: I have heard that the former kings in establishing order arranged the nine domains in sequence, divided borders and drew boundaries, and each kept to his dwelling.
translations.idiomatic: The ancient kings ordered the realm by fixing borders so that each people could dwell in peace.

sentences.zh: 在昔盛世，人無遷業，故井田之制，三代以隆。

translations.literal: In past ages of flourishing rule, men did not change their occupations; thus the well-field system flourished through the Three Dynasties.
translations.idiomatic: In great ages no one left his trade; that is why the well-field system lasted through the Three Dynasties.

sentences.zh: 秦革斯政，漢遂不改，富強兼并，於是為弊。

translations.literal: Qin overturned this policy; Han did not change it, and the strong annexed the rich—thus the abuse arose.
translations.idiomatic: Qin abolished that order; Han kept the change, and the strong swallowed the weak.

sentences.zh: 然九服弗擾，所託成舊，在漢西京，大遷田、景之族，以實關中，即以三輔為鄉閭，不復係之於齊、楚。

translations.literal: Yet the nine domains were not disturbed; what they relied on remained the old. In the Western Han capital, the clans of Tian and Jing were moved on a great scale to fill Guanzhong, and the Three Metropolises became their native hamlets, no longer tied to Qi and Chu.
translations.idiomatic: Still the realm held together because people kept their roots. In Western Han the Tian and Jing clans were moved en masse into Guanzhong; the capital districts became home and they were cut off from Qi and Chu.

sentences.zh: 自永嘉播越，爰託淮、海，朝有匡復之算，民懷思本之心，經略之圖，日不暇給。

translations.literal: From the Yongjia turmoil onward, the court entrusted itself to the Huai and the sea; the court had plans to restore the realm, and the people cherished the wish to return to their roots; schemes of strategy left no day free.
translations.idiomatic: After Yongjia the court fled to the Huai and the sea. All wanted restoration, and the people longed for home, but war left no day for civil rule.

sentences.zh: 是以寧民綏治，猶有未遑。

translations.literal: Thus in settling the people and pacifying rule, there was still no leisure.
translations.idiomatic: Peaceful settlement had to wait.

sentences.zh: 及至大司馬桓溫，以民無定本，傷治為深，庚戌土斷，以一其業。

translations.literal: When Grand Marshal Huan Wen saw that the people had no fixed base and that harm to governance lay deep therein, in the year gengxu he carried out the land register to unify their livelihoods.
translations.idiomatic: When Grand Marshal Huan Wen saw that people had no fixed domicile and government suffered for it, he carried out the gengxu land register in 365 to give everyone a single legal home.

sentences.zh: 于時財阜國豐，實由於此。

translations.literal: At that time wealth flourished and the state was rich—this was truly owing to that measure.
translations.idiomatic: The treasury grew rich because of it.

sentences.zh: 自茲迄今，彌歷年載，畫一之制，漸用頹弛。

translations.literal: From then until now, many years have passed; the unified system has gradually fallen into decay.
translations.idiomatic: Since then the unified system had slowly collapsed.

sentences.zh: 雜居流寓，閭伍弗修，王化所以未純，民瘼所以猶在。

translations.literal: Mixed residence and floating registration, neighborhood registers not kept in order—the royal transformation was therefore not pure, and the people's afflictions therefore remained.
translations.idiomatic: Migrants and false registers broke the wards; government never fully took hold, and the people's misery remained.

sentences.zh: 臣荷重任，恥責實深，自非改調解張，無以濟治。

translations.literal: I bear a heavy commission and am deeply ashamed of the gap between charge and result; unless I change the registers and loosen the bonds, I cannot bring order.
translations.idiomatic: I hold great power and am ashamed that rule still fails. Without fixing the registers I cannot govern.

sentences.zh: 夫人情滯常，難與慮始，所謂父母之邦以為桑梓者，誠以生焉終焉，敬愛所託耳。

translations.literal: Human feeling clings to the constant and finds it hard to plan at the beginning; what is called taking one's native district as one's mulberry tree is truly because one is born and dies there and the object of reverent love is entrusted there.
translations.idiomatic: People cling to habit and hate sudden change. They call their home a mulberry tree because they are born and buried there and their loyalty belongs there.

sentences.zh: 今所居累世，墳壟成行，敬恭之誠，豈不與事而至。

translations.literal: Where they now dwell for generations, graves and mounds stand in rows; the sincerity of reverence—how could it fail to attend upon the matter when it comes?
translations.idiomatic: Families have lived in one place for generations; their graves line the fields. How could they not care when the state asks them to move?

sentences.zh: 請準庚戌土斷之科，庶子本所弘，稍與事著。

translations.literal: I ask that the gengxu land-register statute be applied, so that the intent to honor native roots may be broadly carried out and may gradually show in affairs.
translations.idiomatic: I ask that the gengxu land register be enforced again, so respect for native roots may guide policy.

sentences.zh: 然後率之以仁義，鼓之以威武，超大江而跨黃河，撫九州而復舊土，則戀本之志，乃速申於當年，[3]在始暫勤，要終所以能易。

translations.literal: Then, leading them with benevolence and righteousness and rousing them with martial might, crossing the great river and spanning the Yellow River, comforting the nine provinces and recovering the old lands—then the wish to cherish one's roots would quickly be fulfilled in that year, [3] a brief hardship at the start, but in the end the change could be made easy.
translations.idiomatic: Then, with benevolence and force together, we may cross the Yangtze and Yellow River, recover the north, and give every man his home again. [3] The pain at first will be brief; in the end the change will be easy.

sentences.zh: 伏惟陛下，垂矜萬民，憐其所失，永懷鴻雁之詩，思隆中興之業。

translations.literal: Bow your head, Your Majesty, pitying the myriad people, cherishing what they have lost, ever keeping in mind the ode of the wild geese, thinking to exalt the enterprise of restoration.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty pities the people, remembers what they have lost, and keeps the ode of the wild geese in mind, longing to restore the realm.

sentences.zh: 既委臣以國重，期臣以寧濟，若所啟合允，請付外施行。

translations.literal: Having entrusted me with the weight of the state and expecting me to bring peace, if what I propose is fitting, I ask that it be sent out and put into practice.
translations.idiomatic: You have charged me with the realm and expect peace from me. If this plan is sound, let it be carried out.

sentences.zh: 於是依界土斷，唯徐、兗、青三州居晉陵者，不在斷例。

translations.literal: Thereupon land was registered according to boundaries; only those in Jinling from Xu, Yan, and Qing provinces were outside the statute.
translations.idiomatic: Land was then registered by district. Only households of Xu, Yan, and Qing living in Jinling were exempt.

sentences.zh: 諸流寓郡縣，多被併省。

translations.literal: Many of the floating commanderies and counties were merged or abolished.
translations.idiomatic: Many refugee commanderies and counties were merged or abolished.

sentences.zh: 以公領鎮西將軍、豫州刺史。

translations.literal: He was made General Who Guards the West and Inspector of Yuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu was made General Who Guards the West and Inspector of Yuzhou.

sentences.zh: 公固讓太傅、州牧及班劍，奉還黃鉞。

translations.literal: Gaozu firmly declined Grand Tutor, Governor of the province, and the ceremonial swords, and returned the yellow battle-axe.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu refused the Grand Tutorship, the governorship, and the ceremonial swords, and sent back the yellow battle-axe.

sentences.zh: 七月，朱齡石平蜀，斬偽蜀王譙縱，傳首京師。

translations.literal: In the seventh month, Zhu Lingshi pacified Shu, beheaded the false King of Shu Qiao Zong, and sent his head to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month Zhu Lingshi conquered Shu, killed the pretender Qiao Zong, and sent his head to the capital.

sentences.zh: 九月，封公次子義真為桂陽縣公，以賞平齊及定盧循也。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, Gaozu's second son Yizhen was enfeoffed as Duke of Guiyang, to reward the pacification of Qi and the defeat of Lu Xun.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month Gaozu's second son Yizhen was made Duke of Guiyang, rewarding the conquest of Qi and the defeat of Lu Xun.

sentences.zh: 天子重申前命，授公太傅、揚州牧，加羽葆、鼓吹、班劍二十人。

translations.literal: The Son of Heaven again pressed the earlier appointment: Gaozu was made Grand Tutor and Governor of Yangzhou, with feathered canopy, drums, whistles, and twenty ceremonial swords.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor again pressed the old honors on him: Grand Tutor, Governor of Yangzhou, imperial music, and twenty ceremonial swords.

sentences.zh: 將吏百餘敦勸，乃受羽葆、鼓吹、班劍，餘固辭。

translations.literal: More than a hundred officers urged him earnestly; only then did he accept the feathered canopy, drums, whistles, and ceremonial swords; the rest he firmly declined.
translations.idiomatic: Over a hundred officers begged him to accept. He took the music and swords but refused the rest.

sentences.zh: 十年，息民簡役。

translations.literal: In the tenth year, he gave the people rest and simplified corvée.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year (414) he eased burdens on the people and cut labor duties.

sentences.zh: 築東府，起府舍。

translations.literal: He built the eastern headquarters and raised the official residences.
translations.idiomatic: He built the eastern headquarters and its offices.

sentences.zh: 平西將軍、荊州刺史司馬休之，宗室之重，又得江漢人心，公疑其有異志，而休之兄子譙王文思在京師，招集輕俠，公執文思送還休之，令自為其所。

translations.literal: General Who Pacifies the West and Inspector of Jingzhou Sima Xiuzhi was a man of weight in the imperial clan and had won the hearts of the Jiang and Han regions; Gaozu suspected he harbored a different intent. Xiuzhi's elder brother's son, the Marquis of Qiao Wen Si, was in the capital gathering daredevils; Gaozu seized Wen Si and sent him back to Xiuzhi, telling him to deal with the matter himself.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Xiuzhi, General Who Pacifies the West and Inspector of Jingzhou, was a prince of the blood with a following in Jiang and Han. Gaozu distrusted him. Xiuzhi's nephew Wen Si was in the capital gathering ruffians; Gaozu arrested Wen Si and sent him to Xiuzhi to punish as he saw fit.

sentences.zh: 休之表廢文思，并與公書陳謝。

translations.literal: Xiuzhi memorialized to dismiss Wen Si and also wrote Gaozu a letter of apology.
translations.idiomatic: Xiuzhi memorialized to disown Wen Si and wrote Gaozu to apologize.

sentences.zh: 十一年正月，公收休之子文寶、兄子文祖，並於獄賜死，率眾軍西討。

translations.literal: In the first month of the eleventh year, Gaozu seized Xiuzhi's son Wenbao and his brother's son Wenzu and granted them death in prison, then led the armies west on campaign.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the eleventh year (415) Gaozu had Wenbao and Wenzu executed in prison and marched west.

sentences.zh: 復加黃鉞，[4]領荊州刺史。

translations.literal: He was again given the yellow battle-axe [4] and took charge as Inspector of Jingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was again given the yellow battle-axe [4] and made Inspector of Jingzhou.

sentences.zh: 辛巳，發京師，以中軍將軍道憐監留府事。

translations.literal: On the day xinsi he set out from the capital; Central Army General Daoling oversaw the headquarters left behind.
translations.idiomatic: On the day xinsi he left the capital. Daoling ran affairs at headquarters.

sentences.zh: 休之上表自陳曰：

translations.literal: Xiuzhi memorialized in his own person, saying:
translations.idiomatic: Xiuzhi submitted a personal memorial:

sentences.zh: 臣聞運不常一，治亂代有，陽九既謝，圮終則泰。

translations.literal: I have heard that fortune is not constant, order and disorder succeed each other in turn; when the yang ninth calamity has passed, collapse at the end gives way to peace.
translations.idiomatic: Fortune never stays the same; order and chaos take turns. When the worst is past, ruin gives way to renewal.

sentences.zh: 昔篡臣肆逆，皇綱絕紐，卜世未改，[5]鼎祚再隆。

translations.literal: In former days the usurping minister ran riot, the imperial cords were severed, the allotted age was not yet changed, [5] and the sacred vessel was raised a second time.
translations.idiomatic: Once a usurper seized power and the dynasty seemed dead, yet the throne was restored [5] and the mandate lived again.

sentences.zh: 太尉臣裕威武明斷，道建義旗，除蕩元凶，皇居反正。

translations.literal: Grand Commandant Liu Yu was martially awesome and brilliantly decisive; he raised the banner of righteousness, swept away the chief villain, and restored the imperial palace to right order.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Commandant Liu Yu was fierce and clear-sighted. He raised the righteous standard, destroyed the usurper, and brought the throne back to order.

sentences.zh: 布衣匹夫，匡復社稷，南剿盧循，北定廣固，千載以來，功無與等。

translations.literal: A commoner in plain cloth, he restored the altars of state; south he destroyed Lu Xun, north he pacified Guanggu—in a thousand years, no achievement has equaled his.
translations.idiomatic: Born a commoner, he restored the dynasty; in the south he crushed Lu Xun, in the north he took Guanggu. In a thousand years, no man had matched such feats.

sentences.zh: 由是四海歸美，朝野推崇。

translations.literal: From this the Four Seas turned to praise him, and court and countryside alike exalted him.
translations.idiomatic: All under Heaven sang his praise, and court and country alike held him in awe.

sentences.zh: 既位窮台牧，權傾人主，不能以道處功，恃寵驕溢。

translations.literal: Once he stood at the summit as terrace lord and pasturage minister, his power overawed the sovereign; he could not treat his achievements with the Way, but relied on favor and waxed arrogant beyond measure.
translations.idiomatic: Once he held the highest posts and his power eclipsed the throne, he could not bear his merit with restraint. Swollen by favor, he grew insufferably proud.

sentences.zh: 自以酬賞既極，便情在無上，刑戮逆濫，政用暴苛。

translations.literal: He considered that rewards had reached their limit, and his heart set on being above all; punishments and executions were perverse and excessive, and government was cruel and harsh.
translations.idiomatic: Thinking he had been rewarded to the full, he set his heart on standing above all. Executions ran wild, and his rule turned brutal and harsh.

sentences.zh: 問鼎之迹日彰，人臣之禮頓缺。

translations.literal: The traces of his desire to seize the vessel grew plainer day by day, and the rites owed by a subject were suddenly cast aside.
translations.idiomatic: Day by day his ambition to seize the throne showed more plainly, and the obligations of a subject were cast aside.

sentences.zh: 陛下四時膳御，觸事縣空，宮省供奉，十不一在。

translations.literal: Your Majesty's four-seasons meals and provisions—at every turn the cupboards hung empty; of what the palace offices should supply, not one in ten remained.
translations.idiomatic: Even Your Majesty's meals through the four seasons were left bare; scarcely one item in ten of what the palace should provide ever arrived.

sentences.zh: 皇后寢疾之際，湯藥不周，手與家書，多所求告。

translations.literal: When the Empress lay ill, medicines were not properly provided; by his own hand he wrote family letters with many requests and petitions.
translations.idiomatic: When the Empress lay ill, medicines were wanting, while he wrote personal letters full of demands and pleas.

sentences.zh: 皆是朝士共所聞見，莫不傷懷憤歎，口不敢言。

translations.literal: These were all things the court officials heard and saw together; none failed to ache in heart and sigh in anger, yet none dared speak.
translations.idiomatic: Every courtier saw and heard these things; all grieved and seethed, yet none dared speak aloud.

sentences.zh: 前揚州刺史元顯第五息法興，桓玄之釁，逃遠於外，王路既開，始得歸本。

translations.literal: The fifth son of the former Inspector of Yangzhou Yuan Xian, Faxing, when Huan Xuan's trouble arose, fled far abroad; once the kingly road was opened again, he was at last able to return to his roots.
translations.idiomatic: Faxing, fifth son of the former Yangzhou inspector Yuan Xian, had fled abroad during Huan Xuan's rebellion. Only when the imperial road was open again could he return home.

sentences.zh: 太傅之胤，絕而復興，凡在有懷，誰不感慶。

translations.literal: An heir of the Grand Tutor, cut off and then revived—among all who had hearts, who did not feel moved and rejoice?
translations.idiomatic: A grandson of the Grand Tutor, lost and restored—who with any conscience would not rejoice?

sentences.zh: 裕吞噬之心，不避輕重，以法興聰敏明慧，必為民望所歸，芳蘭既茂，內懷憎惡，乃妄扇異言，無罪即戮。

translations.literal: Yu's heart of devouring showed no regard for weight or light; because Faxing was clever and bright, certain to be where the people's hopes gathered, and the fragrant orchid had already flourished, he harbored hatred within, then groundlessly stirred alien talk and executed him though guiltless.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yu's devouring envy spared no one. Faxing was clever and bright, sure to win the people's hearts; like a flourishing orchid he drew Yu's secret hate. Yu spread false charges and put him to death without cause.

sentences.zh: 大司馬臣德文及王妃公主，情計切逼，並狼狽請命。

translations.literal: The Grand Marshal, your subject Dewen, and the princess consort and imperial princesses—their feelings and plans were pressed to extremity; all alike scrambled to beg for their lives.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Marshal Sima Dewen, the princesses, and the royal ladies were driven to desperation and pleaded for their lives in disorder.

sentences.zh: 逆肆禍毒，誓不矜許，寃酷之痛，感動行路。

translations.literal: The rebel wantonly loosed harm and poison, swearing never to show mercy; the pain of false accusation and cruel injustice moved even those on the road.
translations.idiomatic: The traitor wreaked havoc and refused all mercy. The injustice of it moved even passers-by on the road.

sentences.zh: 自以地卑位重，荷恩崇大，乃以庶孽與德文嫡婚，致茲非偶，實由威逼。

translations.literal: Considering himself low in station but heavy in position, bearing great elevated favor, he then joined a child of a concubine in marriage with Dewen's legitimate daughter, bringing about this ill-matched union—which in truth came from coercive power.
translations.idiomatic: Thinking himself humble in origin yet raised so high, he forced Dewen's legitimate daughter to marry his own bastard son—a grotesque match born of naked intimidation.

sentences.zh: 故衞將軍劉毅、右將軍劉藩、前將軍諸葛長民、尚書僕射謝混、南蠻校尉郗僧施，或盛勳德胤，令望在身，皆社稷輔弼，協讚所寄，無罪無辜，一旦夷滅。

translations.literal: The Defender General Liu Yi, the Right General Liu Fan, the Forward General Zhuge Changmin, the Master of Writing Vice Director Xie Hun, and the Colonel of the Southern Man Xi Sengshi—some were men of towering merit and noble descent, their reputation still upon them; all were pillars of the altars of state, entrusted with joint support—yet without guilt or crime, in a single day they were exterminated.
translations.idiomatic: Defender General Liu Yi, Right General Liu Fan, Forward General Zhuge Changmin, Vice Director of the Masters of Writing Xie Hun, and Colonel of the Southern Man Xi Sengshi—men of great merit and standing, pillars of the realm—were destroyed in a single day, innocent and blameless.

sentences.zh: 猜忍之性，終古所希。

translations.literal: A suspicious and cruel nature such as this is rare in all antiquity.
translations.idiomatic: Such suspicion and cruelty are scarcely known in all history.

sentences.zh: 臣自惟門戶衰破，賴之獲存，皇家所重，終古難匹。

translations.literal: I reflect that my own house has declined and been broken, and that I survive only through reliance on him; the weight the imperial house places on us is unmatched since antiquity.
translations.idiomatic: My own house has fallen into ruin; I survive only through his protection. The throne has placed a weight on us unmatched in history.

sentences.zh: 是以公私歸馮，事盡祗順。

translations.literal: For this reason public and private affairs alike were entrusted to Feng, and in all matters I showed utmost deference.
translations.idiomatic: For this reason public and private affairs alike went through him, and I deferred in everything.

sentences.zh: 再授荊州，輒苦陳告，自以才弱位隆，不宜久荷分陝，屢求解任，必不見聽。

translations.literal: When Jingzhou was conferred on me again, I earnestly petitioned, considering my talent slight and my position lofty, unfit to bear the partition of the two halves long; I repeatedly sought release from office, yet was never heeded.
translations.idiomatic: When Jingzhou was given me again, I pleaded that my talent was slight and my rank too high to bear such a burden long, and asked repeatedly to be relieved—but was never heard.

sentences.zh: 前經攜侍老母，半家俱西，凡諸子姪，悉留京輦。

translations.literal: Earlier I took my aged mother in attendance, half the household going west; all my sons and nephews I left in the capital.
translations.idiomatic: I had brought my aged mother west with half the household, leaving all my sons and nephews in the capital.

sentences.zh: 臣兄子譙王文思，雖年少常人，粗免咎悔，性好交遊，未知防遠，羣醜交構，為其風聲。

translations.literal: My elder brother's son, Prince of Qiao Wang Wensi, though young was no worse than ordinary men and broadly free of blame; his nature loved company and friendship, and he did not know how to guard against distance; the rabble joined plots and made him their talk.
translations.idiomatic: My nephew, Prince of Qiao Wang Wensi, was young but no worse than most men, fond of company and slow to see danger. Schemers made him their pretext.

sentences.zh: 裕遂翦戮人士，遠送文思。

translations.literal: Yu then cut down gentlemen and sent Wensi far away.
translations.idiomatic: Yu then slaughtered the gentry and had Wensi sent far away.

sentences.zh: 臣順其此旨，表送章節，請廢文思，改襲大宗，遣息文寶送女東歸。

translations.literal: I complied with this intent, memorialized with full documents, asked that Wensi be deposed, that the great line be changed in succession, and sent my son Wenbao to escort my daughter east.
translations.idiomatic: I complied: I memorialized to depose Wensi, change the succession, and sent my son Wenbao to escort my daughter east.

sentences.zh: 自謂推誠奉順，理不過此。

translations.literal: I thought that in pushing sincerity and showing compliance, reason could go no further than this.
translations.idiomatic: I believed I had shown every possible loyalty and submission.

sentences.zh: 豈意裕苞藏禍心，遂見討伐，加惡文思，構生罪釁。

translations.literal: Who would have thought Yu harbored a treacherous heart and then came to attack and punish, heaping further crimes on Wensi and fabricating guilt?
translations.idiomatic: Yet Yu harbored treachery all along and now marched against me, heaping false crimes on Wensi.

sentences.zh: 羣小之言，遠近噂𠴲，而臣純愚，闇信必謂不然。

translations.literal: The talk of the petty crowd spread near and far in murmurs, yet I, pure and foolish, trusted in the dark that it could not be so.
translations.idiomatic: Rumors spread far and wide, yet I, foolishly trusting, refused to believe them.

sentences.zh: 尋臣府司馬張茂度狼狽東歸，南平太守檀範之復以此月三日委郡叛逆，尋有審問，東軍已上。

translations.literal: Soon my headquarters Master of Records Zhang Maodu fled east in disorder, and the Governor of Nanping Tan Fanzhi on the third of this month abandoned his commandery in rebellion; there has since been investigation, and the eastern army has already set out.
translations.idiomatic: Soon my chief clerk Zhang Maodu fled east in disarray, and Nanping governor Tan Fanzhi abandoned his post in rebellion on the third of this month. The eastern army is already on the march.

sentences.zh: 裕今此舉，非有怨憎，正以臣王室之幹，位居藩岳，時賢既盡，唯臣獨存，規以翦滅，成其篡殺。

translations.literal: Yu takes this action not from any personal hatred, but simply because I am the trunk of the royal house, holding a frontier lord's position at the top of the screen; when the men of the age are all gone, only I remain—he plans to cut me down and complete his usurpation and slaughter.
translations.idiomatic: This campaign is not born of personal hatred. I am the royal house's mainstay, a great frontier lord; when all others of merit are gone, only I remain. He means to destroy me and complete his usurpation.

sentences.zh: 鎮北將軍臣宗之、青州刺史臣敬宣，並是裕所深忌憚，欲以次除蕩，然後傾移天日，於事可易。

translations.literal: Defender of the North General Zongzhi and Inspector of Qingzhou Jingxuan are both men Yu deeply fears and dreads; he wishes to remove them in turn and then shift the sun and moon—then the affair will be easy.
translations.idiomatic: Defender of the North Zongzhi and Qingzhou inspector Jingxuan are men Yu deeply fears; he means to eliminate them one by one, then seize the throne—and the rest will be easy.

sentences.zh: 今荊、雍義徒，不召而集，子來之眾，其會如林。

translations.literal: Now the righteous bands of Jing and Yong gather without being summoned; the masses come like children, their assembly like a forest.
translations.idiomatic: Now the loyal forces of Jing and Yong rally unbidden; men flock to us like children returning home, thick as a forest.

sentences.zh: 豈臣無德所能綏致，蓋七廟之靈，理貫幽顯。

translations.literal: How could it be that I have virtue enough to bring this about? It is rather the numen of the seven temples, whose principle runs through the hidden and manifest.
translations.idiomatic: Surely this is not my virtue alone, but the spirits of the ancestral shrines, whose justice reaches from this world to the next.

sentences.zh: 輒授文思振武將軍、南郡太守，宗之子竟陵太守魯軌進號輔國將軍。

translations.literal: I have appointed Wensi General Who Quells Martial Affairs and Governor of Nanjun, and Zongzhi's son, the Governor of Jingling Lu Gui, advanced to General Who Assists the State.
translations.idiomatic: I have appointed Wensi General Who Quells Martial Affairs and governor of Nanjun, and Zongzhi's son Jingling governor Lu Gui promoted to General Who Assists the State.

sentences.zh: 臣今與宗之親御大眾，出據江津，案甲抗威，隨宜應赴。

translations.literal: I now, with Zongzhi, personally lead the great host forth and take position at the river crossing; we set armor and resist his might, responding as occasion demands.
translations.idiomatic: I now lead the main force with Zongzhi to the river crossing, armor set and ready to meet whatever comes.

sentences.zh: 今絳旗所指，唯裕兄弟父子而已。

translations.literal: Where the crimson banner points, it is only at Yu and his brothers and sons.
translations.idiomatic: Our crimson banners aim only at Yu and his brothers and sons.

sentences.zh: 須剋蕩寇逆，尋續馳聞。

translations.literal: Once the bandits and rebels are swept away, I shall immediately send further word.
translations.idiomatic: When the rebels are crushed, I shall report at once.

sentences.zh: 由臣輕弱，致裕凌橫，上慚俯愧，無以厝顏。

translations.literal: Because I am slight and weak, Yu has grown overbearing; above I am ashamed, below I cannot set my face.
translations.idiomatic: My own weakness has let Yu grow arrogant; I am ashamed before Heaven and cannot hold up my head.

sentences.zh: 休之府錄事參軍韓延之，故吏也，有幹用才能。

translations.literal: Xiuzhi's headquarters Record-keeping Adjutant Han Yanzhi was a former subordinate, capable and talented.
translations.idiomatic: Xiuzhi's chief clerk Han Yanzhi, a former subordinate, was capable and talented.

sentences.zh: 公未至江陵，密使與之書曰：「文思事源，遠近所知，去秋遣康之送還司馬君者，[6]推至公之極也。

translations.literal: Before the Duke reached Jiangling, he secretly sent him a letter saying: "The source of the Wensi affair is known near and far; last autumn, when Kangzhi was sent to return him to the Master of Records, [6] that was pushing favor to the utmost.
translations.idiomatic: Before Gaozu reached Jiangling, he secretly wrote to him: "The Wensi affair is known to all. Last autumn, when I sent Kangzhi to return him to your clerk, [6] that was the utmost concession.

sentences.zh: 而了不遜愧，又無表疏。

translations.literal: Yet he showed not the least shame, nor submitted any memorial.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he showed no shame and sent no memorial.

sentences.zh: 文思經正不反，此是天地之不容。

translations.literal: Wensi, having been corrected and not returning—this is what Heaven and Earth cannot contain.
translations.idiomatic: Wensi was corrected and still would not return—that Heaven and Earth cannot abide.

sentences.zh: 吾受命西討，止其父子而已。

translations.literal: I have received the mandate to campaign west and aim only at father and sons.
translations.idiomatic: I march west by imperial command, and my target is only father and son.

sentences.zh: 彼土僑舊，為所驅逼，一無所問。

translations.literal: The old settlers of that land, driven by force, are not to be questioned at all.
translations.idiomatic: The local gentry, forced into this, will not be punished.

sentences.zh: 往年郗僧施、謝邵、任集之等，交構積歲，專為劉毅謀主，所以至此。

translations.literal: In former years Xi Sengshi, Xie Shao, Ren Jizhi, and others plotted together for years, serving exclusively as Liu Yi's chief strategists—hence things came to this.
translations.idiomatic: For years Xi Sengshi, Xie Shao, Ren Jizhi, and others plotted for Liu Yi—that is how we came here.

sentences.zh: 卿等諸人，一時逼迫，本無纖釁。

translations.literal: You and the others were for a time under pressure; originally there was not the slightest fault.
translations.idiomatic: You were pressed for a time; you had no real guilt.

sentences.zh: 吾處懷期物，自有由來。

translations.literal: My heart in embracing men looks to what is to come, and has its reasons from of old.
translations.idiomatic: I judge men by what they may yet do; that has always been my way.

sentences.zh: 今在近路，正是諸人歸身之日。

translations.literal: Now on the near road is precisely the day for you all to return to yourselves.
translations.idiomatic: Now, on the eve of battle, is the day for you to come back to yourselves.

sentences.zh: 若大軍登道，交鋒接刃，蘭艾吾誠不分。

translations.literal: If the great army takes the road and blades meet in clash, I truly make no distinction between orchid and mugwort.
translations.idiomatic: If the armies meet in battle, I will not spare orchid for mugwort.

sentences.zh: 故具示意，并示同懷諸人。

translations.literal: Therefore I set forth my meaning in full and show it to those of like heart among you.
translations.idiomatic: I state this plainly and show it to all who share your plight.

sentences.zh: 」延之報曰：

translations.literal: Yanzhi replied:
translations.idiomatic: Han Yanzhi replied:

sentences.zh: 承親率戎馬，遠履西畿，闔境士庶，莫不恇駭。

translations.literal: I have received that you personally lead war-horses and have come far into the western domain; throughout the commandery, scholars and commoners—none fail to be struck with terror.
translations.idiomatic: Word has come that you lead your army deep into the west; every man in the region is struck with terror.

sentences.zh: 何者？

translations.literal: Why?
translations.idiomatic: Why?

sentences.zh: 莫知師出之名故也。

translations.literal: None knows the name for which the army goes forth.
translations.idiomatic: Because no one knows why your army marches.

sentences.zh: 今辱來疏，始知以譙王前事，良增歎息。

translations.literal: Now, shamed by your letter, I learn at last that it is on account of the Prince of Qiao's former affair—how this increases my sighs.
translations.idiomatic: Your letter shames me into learning at last that this is about the Prince of Qiao—how that deepens my grief.

sentences.zh: 司馬平西體國忠貞，欵愛待物，當於古人中求耳。

translations.literal: The Western Campaigning Marshal in his person serves the state with loyalty and sincerity, treats men with generous affection—one should seek such a man among the ancients.
translations.idiomatic: Marshal Sima Xiuzhi serves the state with loyal heart and treats men with generous affection—such a man belongs among the ancients.

sentences.zh: 以君公有匡復之勳，家國蒙賴，推德委誠，每事詢仰。

translations.literal: Because you, my lord, had the achievement of restoration, and the house and state relied on you, he entrusted virtue and gave sincerity, in every affair seeking your counsel.
translations.idiomatic: Because you restored the dynasty and the realm relied on you, he trusted you utterly and sought your counsel in everything.

sentences.zh: 譙王往以微事見劾，猶自表遜位；

translations.literal: The Prince of Qiao, when before he was impeached on a small matter, still memorialized in his own person to yield his place;
translations.idiomatic: When the Prince of Qiao was charged on a minor matter, he still offered to step down;

sentences.zh: 況以大過而當默然邪。

translations.literal: how much more, when the fault was great, could he remain silent?
translations.idiomatic: how then could he stay silent when the charge was grave?

sentences.zh: 但康之前言有所不盡，故重使胡道諮白所懷。

translations.literal: Only Kangzhi's earlier words did not say everything, so he again sent Hu Daozhi to speak plainly what was in his heart.
translations.idiomatic: Kangzhi's earlier message did not say all; so he sent Hu Daozhi to speak his mind plainly.

sentences.zh: 道未及反，已奏表廢之，所不盡者命耳。

translations.literal: The envoy had not yet returned when a memorial was already submitted to depose him—what was not said was settled by fate alone.
translations.idiomatic: Before the envoy returned, you had already memorialized to depose him—what was left unsaid was settled by your will alone.

sentences.zh: 推寄相與之懷，正當如此？

translations.literal: Is this how one should treat mutual trust?
translations.idiomatic: Is this how trust between you was meant to work?

sentences.zh: 有何不可，便興兵戈。

translations.literal: What could not be borne, that you should at once raise arms?
translations.idiomatic: What could not wait, that you must raise arms at once?

sentences.zh: 自義旗秉權以來，四方方伯，誰敢不先相諮疇，而逕表天子邪。

translations.literal: Since the righteous banner took power, which frontier lord has dared not first consult you, yet go straight to memorializing the Son of Heaven?
translations.idiomatic: Since you took power, which frontier lord has dared report to the throne without consulting you first?

sentences.zh: 譙王為宰相所責，又表廢之，經正何歸，表使何因，可謂「欲加之罪，其無辭乎」！

translations.literal: The Prince of Qiao was rebuked by the chief minister and again memorialized to be deposed—where does rectitude lie, what cause does the memorial have? One may say, "When you wish to condemn a man, you will find the words."
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Qiao was charged by the chief minister and deposed by memorial—where is the justice, what is the ground? Truly: "When you wish to condemn a man, you will find the words."

sentences.zh: 劉裕足下，海內之人，誰不見足下此心，而復欲欺誑國士！

translations.literal: Liu Yu, beneath Heaven—who does not see this heart of yours, yet you would again deceive and beguile the men of the state!
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yu, all under Heaven see your heart—yet you would still deceive the realm!

sentences.zh: 天地所不容，在彼不在此矣。

translations.literal: What Heaven and Earth cannot contain lies with you, not with us.
translations.idiomatic: What Heaven and Earth cannot abide is on your side, not ours.

sentences.zh: 來示言「處懷期物，自有由來」。

translations.literal: Your letter says, "My heart in embracing men looks to what is to come, and has its reasons from of old."
translations.idiomatic: You write, "I judge men by what they may yet do; that has always been my way."

sentences.zh: 今伐人之君，啗人以利，真可謂「處懷期物，自有由來」者矣。

translations.literal: Now you attack another's lord and feed men with profit—truly one may say, "My heart in embracing men looks to what is to come, and has its reasons from of old."
translations.idiomatic: Now you attack a lord and bait men with profit—yes, that is "judging men by what they may yet do."

sentences.zh: 劉藩死於閶闔之內，諸葛斃於左右之手，甘言詫方伯，襲之以輕兵，遂使席上靡款懷之士，閫外無自信諸侯，以是為得算，良可恥也。

translations.literal: Liu Fan died within the palace gate, Zhuge perished at the hands of those beside you; sweet words deceived the frontier lords, and light troops fell upon them—so that within the hall there were no men of sincere heart, and beyond the gates no lords who trusted themselves. To call this winning the reckoning is truly shameful.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Fan died at the palace gate, Zhuge at the hands of your intimates. You lured frontier lords with sweet words, then struck with light troops—so that within the court no man dared speak honestly, and beyond the gates no lord felt secure. To call that strategy is shameful indeed.

sentences.zh: 貴府將佐及朝廷賢德，寄性命以過日，心企太平久矣。

translations.literal: The generals and aides of your headquarters and the worthy men of the court stake their lives day by day, their hearts long set on peace.
translations.idiomatic: Your officers and the court's worthies stake their lives each day, longing for peace.

sentences.zh: 吾誠鄙劣，嘗聞道於君子。

translations.literal: I am indeed base and inferior, yet I have heard the Way from gentlemen.
translations.idiomatic: I am base and low, yet I have heard the Way from gentlemen.

sentences.zh: 以平西之至德，寧可無授命之臣乎！

translations.literal: With the Western Campaigning Marshal's utmost virtue, could there be no minister who would give his life in command?
translations.idiomatic: With Marshal Xiuzhi's supreme virtue, could he lack men who would die for him?

sentences.zh: 未能自投虎口，比迹郗、任之徒明矣。

translations.literal: That I could not throw myself into the tiger's maw makes me clearly unlike Xi, Ren, and their kind.
translations.idiomatic: That I will not throw myself into the tiger's maw sets me clearly apart from Xi and Ren and their like.

sentences.zh: 假令天長喪亂，九流渾濁，當與臧洪遊於地下，不復多言。

translations.literal: Even if Heaven long prolongs disorder and the nine streams run turbid, I shall wander underground with Zang Hong—no more words.
translations.idiomatic: Even if chaos endures and the world runs foul, I shall keep company underground with Zang Hong—and say no more.

sentences.zh: 公視書歎息，以示諸佐曰：「事人當如此。」

translations.literal: The Duke read the letter and sighed, showing it to his aides and saying: "To serve a man should be like this."
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu read the letter, sighed, and showed it to his staff: "To serve a lord should be like this."

sentences.zh: 三月，軍次江陵。

translations.literal: In the third month the army halted at Jiangling.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month the army reached Jiangling.

sentences.zh: 初雍州刺史魯宗之常慮不為公所容，與休之相結，至是率其子竟陵太守軌會于江陵。

translations.literal: Earlier the Inspector of Yongzhou Lu Zongzhi had often feared he would not be tolerated by the Duke; he allied with Xiuzhi, and now led his son, the Governor of Jingling Gui, to join Xiuzhi at Jiangling.
translations.idiomatic: Yongzhou inspector Lu Zongzhi had long feared Gaozu would not tolerate him; allied with Xiuzhi, he now brought his son Jingling governor Gui to join him at Jiangling.

sentences.zh: 江夏太守劉虔之邀之，軍敗見殺。

translations.literal: The Governor of Jiangxia Liu Qianzhi intercepted him; his army was defeated and he was killed.
translations.idiomatic: Jiangxia governor Liu Qianzhi intercepted them; Zongzhi was defeated and killed.

sentences.zh: 公命彭城內史徐逵之、參軍王允之出江夏口，復為軌所敗，並沒。

translations.literal: The Duke ordered the Administrator of Pengcheng Interior Xu Daizhi and the Adjutant Wang Yunzhi to go out to the Jiangxia mouth; they were again defeated by Gui and both perished.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu sent Pengcheng interior administrator Xu Daizhi and adjutant Wang Yunzhi to the Jiangxia crossing; Gui defeated them and both were lost.

sentences.zh: 時公軍泊馬頭，即日率眾軍濟江，躬督諸將登岸，莫不奮踊爭先。

translations.literal: At that time the Duke's army was moored at Matou; that same day he led the host across the river, personally supervising the generals as they went ashore—none failed to leap forward striving to be first.
translations.idiomatic: The army lay at Matou; that same day Gaozu led the host across the river and personally supervised the landing—every man strove to be first ashore.

sentences.zh: 休之眾潰，與軌等奔襄陽，江陵平。

translations.literal: Xiuzhi's host collapsed; with Gui and the others he fled to Xiangyang, and Jiangling was pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Xiuzhi's army collapsed; he fled with Gui and others to Xiangyang, and Jiangling was pacified.

sentences.zh: 加領南蠻校尉。

translations.literal: He was further appointed Colonel of the Southern Man.
translations.idiomatic: He was further made Colonel of the Southern Man.

sentences.zh: 將拜，值四廢日，佐史鄭鮮之、褚叔度、王弘、傅亮白遷日，不許。

translations.literal: When he was about to take office, it fell on a day of the four prohibitions; the clerks Zheng Xianzhi, Chu Shudu, Wang Hong, and Fu Liang asked to move the day—the request was not granted.
translations.idiomatic: On taking office the day fell among the four prohibited days; clerks Zheng Xianzhi, Chu Shudu, Wang Hong, and Fu Liang asked to postpone it—he refused.

sentences.zh: 下書曰：「此州積弊，事故相仍，民疲田蕪，杼軸空匱。

translations.literal: An edict said: "This province has long accumulated abuses, affairs and troubles succeeding one another; the people are weary, the fields overgrown, and the loom's axle stands empty.
translations.idiomatic: An edict said: "This province has long been abused, troubles piled one on another; the people are worn out, fields lie fallow, and the treasury is empty.

sentences.zh: 加以舊章乖昧，事役頻苦，童耄奪養，老稚服戎，空戶從役，或越紼應召。

translations.literal: Moreover old regulations are confused and obscure, corvée and service are frequent and bitter; the very young are robbed of nurture, old and young don armor; empty households follow service, some even answering the summons before the mourning cloth is removed.
translations.idiomatic: Regulations are confused, corvée endless; children are robbed of care, old and young bear arms; empty households are pressed into service, some called up before mourning is done.

sentences.zh: 每永懷民瘼，宵分忘寢，誠宜蠲除苛政，弘茲簡惠。

translations.literal: Whenever I forever cherish the people's afflictions, I forget sleep at midnight; truly we should abolish harsh government and extend this simple favor.
translations.idiomatic: I brood on the people's suffering and lose sleep at midnight; harsh rule must be abolished and simple mercy extended.

sentences.zh: 庶令凋風弊政，與事而新，寧一之化，成於朞月。

translations.literal: May the withered wind and corrupt government be renewed with the affair; may the transformation of repose in unity be accomplished within a month.
translations.idiomatic: May corrupt ways be made new with this change; may peace be restored within a month.

sentences.zh: 荊、雍二州，西局、蠻府吏及軍人年十二以還，六十以上，及扶養孤幼，單丁大艱，悉仰遣之。

translations.literal: In the two provinces Jing and Yong, clerks of the western bureau and the southern-barbarian headquarters, and soldiers aged twelve and above, sixty and below, and those nurturing orphans and the young, single men in great hardship—all are to be sent home.
translations.idiomatic: In Jing and Yong, clerks of the western bureau and southern-barbarian office, and soldiers twelve and over, sixty and under, and those nursing orphans, widows, or in grave hardship—all are dismissed.

sentences.zh: 窮獨不能存者，給其長賑。

translations.literal: Those destitute and alone who cannot survive shall be given long-term relief.
translations.idiomatic: Those too poor to live shall receive long-term relief.

sentences.zh: 府州久勤將吏，依勞銓序。

translations.literal: Officers and clerks of the headquarters and provinces who have long served shall be ranked according to merit.
translations.idiomatic: Officers and clerks who have served long shall be promoted by merit.

sentences.zh: 并除今年租稅。」

translations.literal: This year's land tax is also remitted."
translations.idiomatic: This year's taxes are also remitted."

sentences.zh: 四月，公復率眾進討，至襄陽，休之奔羌。

translations.literal: In the fourth month the Duke again led the host forward on campaign; reaching Xiangyang, Xiuzhi fled to the Qiang.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month Gaozu advanced again; reaching Xiangyang, Xiuzhi fled to the Qiang.

sentences.zh: 天子復重申前命，授太傅、揚州牧，劍履上殿，入朝不趨，贊拜不名，加前部羽葆、鼓吹，置左右長史、司馬、從事中郎四人。

translations.literal: The Son of Heaven again earnestly repeated the former commands, appointing Grand Tutor and Governor of Yangzhou, sword and shoes in the hall, no need to hurry in court audience, bowing in praise without giving his name, adding the former feather canopy and guard of honor, and four each of Senior and Junior Masters of Records and Adjutants.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor again repeated the former honors: Grand Tutor, Governor of Yangzhou, sword and shoes in the hall, no need to hurry in audience, bowing without giving his name, the feather canopy and guard of honor as before, and four Senior and Junior Masters of Records and adjutants.

sentences.zh: 封公第三子義隆為北彭城縣公。

translations.literal: The Duke's third son Yilong was enfeoffed as Duke of Northern Pengcheng county.
translations.idiomatic: His third son Yilong was enfeoffed as Duke of Northern Pengcheng.

sentences.zh: 以中軍將軍道憐為荊州刺史。

translations.literal: Central Army General Daoling was made Inspector of Jingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Central Army General Daoling was made inspector of Jingzhou.

sentences.zh: 八月甲子，公至自江陵，奉還黃鉞，固辭太傅、州牧、前部羽葆、鼓吹，其餘受命。

translations.literal: On the day jiazi in the eighth month the Duke returned from Jiangling, presented back the yellow battle-axe, and firmly declined Grand Tutor, Governor of Yangzhou, the feather canopy and guard of honor; the rest he accepted.
translations.idiomatic: On the day jiazi in the eighth month Gaozu returned from Jiangling, returned the yellow battle-axe, and declined Grand Tutor, Governor of Yangzhou, and the feather canopy and guard of honor; the rest he accepted.

sentences.zh: 朝議以公道尊勳重，不宜復施敬護軍，既加殊禮，奏事不復稱名。

translations.literal: Court discussion held that the Duke's Way was lofty and his merit weighty, and that it was not fitting again to show respect to the Protector Army; since extraordinary honors had been added, in memorials he was no longer to give his name.
translations.idiomatic: The court held that Gaozu's merit was too great to show respect to the Protector Army; with such honors, memorials no longer bore his name.

sentences.zh: 以世子為兗州刺史。

translations.literal: The heir was made Inspector of Yanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The heir was made inspector of Yanzhou.

sentences.zh: 十二年正月，詔公依舊辟士。

translations.literal: In the first month of the twelfth year, an edict ordered the Duke to recruit scholars as before.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the twelfth year an edict ordered him to recruit scholars as before.

sentences.zh: 加領平北將軍、兗州刺史。

translations.literal: He was further appointed General Who Pacifies the North and Inspector of Yanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was further made General Who Pacifies the North and inspector of Yanzhou.

sentences.zh: 增都督南秦，凡二十二州。

translations.literal: His area of supervision was increased to include Southern Qin, twenty-two provinces in all.
translations.idiomatic: His supervision was extended to Southern Qin, twenty-two provinces in all.

sentences.zh: 公以平北文武寡少，不宜別置。

translations.literal: The Duke considered that the civil and military officials of Pacifier of the North were few and insufficient, and that a separate establishment was unsuitable.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu judged the Pacifier of the North too thinly staffed to warrant a separate office.

sentences.zh: 於是罷平北府，以併大府。

translations.literal: Thereupon he abolished the Pacifier of the North headquarters and merged it into the grand headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: He abolished the Pacifier of the North headquarters and merged it into the main command.

sentences.zh: 以世子為豫州刺史。

translations.literal: The heir was made Inspector of Yuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The heir was made inspector of Yuzhou.

sentences.zh: 三月，加公中外大都督。

translations.literal: In the third month, the Duke was further made Grand Commander of All Affairs Within and Without.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month Gaozu was made Grand Commander over all civil and military affairs.

sentences.zh: 初公平齊，仍有定關、洛之意，值盧循侵逼，故其事不諧。

translations.literal: When the Duke had first pacified Qi, he still intended to settle Guan and Luo; as it happened Lu Xun pressed in invasion, so the matter did not succeed.
translations.idiomatic: After pacifying Qi he still meant to retake the Guan and Luo region, but Lu Xun's invasion forced him to set that plan aside.

sentences.zh: 荊、雍既平，方謀外略。

translations.literal: Once Jing and Yong were pacified, he then planned outward expansion.
translations.idiomatic: With Jing and Yong secure, he turned to campaigns beyond the borders.

sentences.zh: 會羌主姚興死，子泓立，兄弟相殺，關中擾亂，公乃戒嚴北討。

translations.literal: It happened that the Qiang ruler Yao Xing died; his son Hong was installed; brothers killed one another; Guanzhong was disturbed and in disorder; the Duke thereupon put the army on alert and campaigned north.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Xing of the Qiang died; his son Hong took the throne; brothers turned on one another and Guanzhong fell into chaos. Gaozu mobilized for a northern campaign.

sentences.zh: 加領征西將軍、司豫二州刺史。

translations.literal: He was further appointed General Who Campaigns West and Inspector of the two provinces Si and Yu.
translations.idiomatic: He was further made General Who Campaigns West and inspector of Si and Yu.

sentences.zh: 以世子為徐、兗二州刺史。

translations.literal: The heir was made Inspector of the two provinces Xu and Yan.
translations.idiomatic: The heir was made inspector of Xu and Yan.

sentences.zh: 下書曰：「吾倡大義，首自本州，克復皇祚，遂建勳烈，外夷勍敵，內清姦軌，皆邦人州黨竭誠盡力之效也。

translations.literal: He issued a document saying: "I raised the great cause, beginning from this province, restored the imperial succession, and thus established meritorious achievement; the foreign barbarians and fierce foes without, and the cleaning of traitors and evil within—all were the effect of the men of the province and the clans giving their utmost loyalty and strength.
translations.idiomatic: He issued a proclamation: "I raised the great cause from this province, restored the throne, and built a record of merit. Clearing foreign enemies abroad and traitors at home—all this came from the whole province giving its utmost loyalty and strength.

sentences.zh: 情若風霜，義貫金石。

translations.literal: Affection like frost and wind, righteousness piercing through metal and stone.
translations.idiomatic: Your loyalty has been fierce as frost and wind; your righteousness, firm as metal and stone.

sentences.zh: 今當奉辭西斾，有事關、河，弱嗣叨蒙，復忝今授，情事纏綿，可謂深矣。

translations.literal: Now, about to take leave with the western banner and take action at Guan and the Yellow River, my weak heir undeservedly receives favor, and again is unworthily given the present appointment—feelings and affairs entwined, it may be called deep indeed.
translations.idiomatic: I now take leave to march west toward Guan and the River, while my young heir undeservedly receives this new burden—our bonds of duty and feeling run very deep indeed.

sentences.zh: 頃軍國務殷，刑辟未息，眷言懷之，能不多歎。

translations.literal: Recently military and state affairs have been pressing, and punishments and executions have not ceased; looking back with remembrance, how could one not sigh greatly?
translations.idiomatic: Affairs of war and state have pressed hard of late, and executions have not ceased. Thinking on this, how can I not sigh?

sentences.zh: 其犯罪繫五歲以還，可一原遣。

translations.literal: Those whose crimes date from imprisonment five years back may all be pardoned and released.
translations.idiomatic: Prisoners convicted five years ago or earlier may all be pardoned and released.

sentences.zh: 文武勞滿未蒙榮轉者，便隨班序報。」

translations.literal: Civil and military men whose service is complete yet who have not received promotion in honor may immediately be registered according to rank and roster."
translations.idiomatic: Civil and military officers who have completed their terms but have not yet been promoted shall be advanced according to rank."

sentences.zh: 公受中外都督及司州，並辭大司馬琅邪王禮敬，朝議從之。

translations.literal: When the Duke received the grand commandership within and without and Si province, he together declined the ceremonial respect due to the Grand Marshal, the Prince of Langye, and court discussion followed this.
translations.idiomatic: On accepting grand command of all affairs and Si province, Gaozu also declined ceremonial obeisance to the Grand Marshal, Prince of Langye; the court agreed.

sentences.zh: 公欲以義聲懷遠，奉琅邪王北伐。

translations.literal: The Duke wished to win the distant regions with the sound of righteousness, and escorted the Prince of Langye on the northern expedition.
translations.idiomatic: Wishing to win distant peoples by righteous example, Gaozu escorted the Prince of Langye on the northern campaign.

sentences.zh: 五月，羌偽黃門侍郎尹沖率兄弟歸順。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, Yin Chong, the Qiang pretender's Yellow Gate Attendant, led his brothers in submission.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month Yin Chong, Attendant at the Yellow Gate to the Qiang pretender, came over with his brothers.

sentences.zh: 又加公北雍州刺史，前部羽葆、鼓吹，增班劍為四十人。

translations.literal: The Duke was further made Inspector of Northern Yongzhou, given front feather canopy and drums and pipes, and his ceremonial swords were increased to forty men.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu was further made inspector of Northern Yongzhou, granted an imperial feather canopy and drums, and forty ceremonial swords.

sentences.zh: 解中書監。

translations.literal: He was relieved of Supervisor of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: He was relieved of the post of Supervisor of the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 八月丁巳，率大眾發京師。

translations.literal: On the day disi of the eighth month he led the great host forth from the capital.
translations.idiomatic: On the day disi in the eighth month he led the main army out of the capital.

sentences.zh: 以世子為中軍將軍，監太尉留府事。

translations.literal: The heir was made General of the Central Army and overseer of the Grand Marshal's duties left behind at the headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: The heir was made General of the Central Army and left to oversee affairs at headquarters.

sentences.zh: 尚書右僕射劉穆之為左僕射，領監軍、中軍二府軍司，入居東府，總攝內外。

translations.literal: Liu Muzhi, Vice Director of the Masters of Writing on the Right, became Left Vice Director, concurrently held the military adjunct posts of the Supervising Army and Central Army headquarters, entered and dwelled in the Eastern Headquarters, and took overall charge within and without.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Muzhi, Vice Director of the Masters of Writing, was promoted to Left Vice Director, made military adjutant to the supervising and central armies, moved into the Eastern Headquarters, and took overall charge of internal and external affairs.

sentences.zh: 九月，公次于彭城，加領徐州刺史。

translations.literal: In the ninth month the Duke halted at Pengcheng and was further appointed Inspector of Xuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month Gaozu halted at Pengcheng and was further made inspector of Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 先是遣冠軍將軍檀道濟、龍驤將軍王鎮惡步向許、洛，羌緣道屯守，皆望風降服。

translations.literal: Earlier he had sent Champion General Tan Daoji and Flying Dragon General Wang Zhen'e by land toward Xu and Luo; the Qiang garrisoned along the route all saw the wind and submitted.
translations.idiomatic: He had earlier sent Champion General Tan Daoji and Flying Dragon General Wang Zhen'e toward Xu and Luoyang by land; Qiang garrisons along the route surrendered at the first approach.

sentences.zh: 偽兗州刺史韋華先據倉垣，亦率眾歸順。

translations.literal: Wei Hua, the pretender's Inspector of Yanzhou, had earlier held Cangyuan and also led his multitude in submission.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Hua, the pretender's inspector of Yanzhou, who had held Cangyuan, also came over with his troops.

sentences.zh: 公又遣北兗州刺史王仲德先以水軍入河。

translations.literal: The Duke again sent Wang Zhongde, Inspector of Northern Yanzhou, ahead with the water army into the river.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu also sent Northern Yanzhou inspector Wang Zhongde ahead with the fleet into the river.

sentences.zh: 仲德破索虜於東郡涼城，進平滑臺。

translations.literal: Zhongde defeated the Suo barbarians at Liangcheng in Dong commandery and advanced peacefully to take Pingtai.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongde defeated the northern barbarians at Liangcheng in Dong commandery and took Pingtai.

sentences.zh: 十月，眾軍至洛陽，圍金墉。

translations.literal: In the tenth month the multitudinous armies reached Luoyang and besieged Jinyong.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month the armies reached Luoyang and besieged Jinyong.

sentences.zh: 泓弟偽平南將軍洸請降，送于京師。

translations.literal: Hong's younger brother, the pretender's General Who Pacifies the South Guang, requested surrender and was sent to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Hong's brother Guang, the pretender's General Who Pacifies the South, surrendered and was sent to the capital.

sentences.zh: 修復晉五陵，置守衞。

translations.literal: The five Jin mausoleums were repaired and restored, and guards were set.
translations.idiomatic: The five Jin imperial tombs were restored and placed under guard.

sentences.zh: 天子詔曰：

translations.literal: The Son of Heaven's edict said:
translations.idiomatic: The emperor's edict said:

sentences.zh: 夫嵩、岱配極，則乾道增輝，藩嶽作屏，則帝王成務。

translations.literal: When Song and Dai match the pole, then the Way of Heaven adds brilliance; when frontier peaks serve as screen, then the tasks of emperors and kings are accomplished.
translations.idiomatic: When Song and Tai stand as the earth's pillars, Heaven's radiance grows; when border mountains serve as the throne's screen, the ruler's work is done.

sentences.zh: 是以夏、殷資昆、彭之伯，有周倚齊、晉之輔。

translations.literal: For this reason Xia and Yin drew on the lords Kun and Peng; Zhou relied on the aides of Qi and Jin.
translations.idiomatic: Thus Xia and Yin leaned on lords like Kun and Peng; Zhou depended on aides from Qi and Jin.

sentences.zh: 鑒諸前典，儀刑萬代，翼治扶危，靡不由此。

translations.literal: Looking to the former canons, a model for ten thousand generations—supporting governance and sustaining peril—none fails to proceed from this.
translations.idiomatic: The ancient records show it: helpers who steady the throne and rescue the realm have always been the pattern for all ages.

sentences.zh: 太尉公命世天縱，齊聖廣淵，明燭四方，道光宇宙。

translations.literal: The Grand Marshal Duke, destiny's man and Heaven-entrusted, equal to the sage and broad and deep, bright illuminates the four quarters, his Way shines through the cosmos.
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Marshal Gaozu is heaven-sent—a sage's breadth and depth, whose light reaches the four quarters and whose virtue fills the cosmos.

sentences.zh: 爰自□□初迪，則投懃王國，妖蝥孔熾，則功存社稷。

translations.literal: From □□ at the first advancement, then he poured effort into the royal domain; when the evil locusts were greatly rampant, then his achievement preserved the altars of state.
translations.idiomatic: From □□ at the outset he gave himself wholly to the royal cause; when disaster ran wild, his merit preserved the dynasty.

sentences.zh: 固以四維是荷，萬邦攸賴者矣。

translations.literal: Truly he bore the four bonds on his shoulders—a man on whom the myriad states relied.
translations.idiomatic: He bore the four pillars of the realm on his shoulders; all the states depended on him.

sentences.zh: 暨桓玄僭逆，傾蕩四海，公深秉大節，靈武霆震，弘濟朕躬，再造王室。

translations.literal: When Huan Xuan usurped in rebellion and overturned and swept the Four Seas, the Duke deeply upheld the great constancy; spirit and martial virtue thundered and shook; broadly rescued Our person; and again made the royal house.
translations.idiomatic: When Huan Xuan rebelled and plunged the realm into chaos, Gaozu held fast to supreme loyalty; his power shook the land like thunder, saved the throne, and remade the dynasty.

sentences.zh: 每惟勳德，銘于厥心，遂北清海、岱，南夷百越，荊、雍稽服，庸、岷順軌，剋黜方難，式遏寇虐。

translations.literal: Ever mindful of his feats and virtue, engraved in Our heart—thereupon north he cleared Hai and Dai, south he subjugated the hundred Yue; Jing and Yong bowed in submission; Yong and Min followed the track; he overcame and removed regional troubles and checked and halted invaders and tyrants.
translations.idiomatic: His merit is engraved on Our heart: he cleared the north to the sea and Mount Tai, pacified the southern Yue, brought Jing and Yong to heel, opened Yong and Min to the royal road, quelled regional rebellion, and checked foreign plunderers.

sentences.zh: 及阿衡王猷，班序內外，仰興絕風，傍嗣逸業。

translations.literal: And as balancer of the ruler's plans, he ordered ranks within and without, looked upward to revive the extinguished style, and alongside succeeded to the lingering enterprise.
translations.idiomatic: As chief minister he ordered court and realm, revived fallen traditions, and carried forward the unfinished work of the throne.

sentences.zh: 秉禮以整俗，遵王以垂訓，聲教遠被，無思不洽。
